content:
Alex: incident-bot just paged — GPU-pool queue spiked, autoscaler failing to add nodes. Seeing sustained queue growth for 35m.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: gpu-capacity-exhausted (high queue length > 200) — severity: P1. Notified oncall.

Alex: quick context — inference queue on `gpu-pool` up from ~20 -> ~650. Backend returning 429s and long tail latency. Autoscaler repeatedly attempts to create nodes but they never join Ready state. ASG shows new instances in ec2, but k8s shows no registration.

Sophie: logs from cluster-autoscaler (excerpt):
```
I0324 09:12:01.123456 1 scale_up.go:423] Scale-up triggered: need 10 nodes
I0324 09:12:02.654321 1 aws_cloud_provider.go:312] CreateNodeGroup: launchTemplateVersion "lt-0f..." rejected: AMI not supported: driver mismatch
I0324 09:12:05.000000 1 scale_up.go:512] ScaleUpError: created instance but failed to register: kubelet kubelet: node never registered
```

Maria: aws console shows ASG launching instances with launch-template version v3. That LT references AMI `ami-0gpu-deprecated` — we rolled a new AMI last week but LT didn't get updated in the infra change. Instances boot with older NVIDIA driver that fails kubelet bootstrapping (CRI handshake fails).

Kevin: also seeing rate limit errors on AWS CreateLaunchTemplateVersion API from terraform-runner just before failures — backlog of infra ops changed earlier may have left LT in inconsistent state.

Alex: customer impact — inference request success rate dropped to ~60% last 30m; 5 top customers seeing increased latency and some request errors. Console alert for SLO breaches fired (p99 > 3s).

Support Ops: We've opened support tickets for top 3 customers, telling them we are actively remediating and routing lower-tier traffic to smaller hosted model.

Sophie: mitigation plan I tried: 1) attempted to manually replace LT on ASG to point at the new AMI by creating a new launch template version and update-asg, 2) created a single spot node (cpu-backed) as temporary capacity to drain non-GPU work. ASG accepted LT update but new instances still failed to register because kubelet crashloop due to nvidia-driver mismatch in AMI.

Alex: immediate actions:
- Roll a new launch template version with correct AMI and user-data that includes the fix (driver install + kubelet extra args). Command used: `aws ec2 create-launch-template-version --launch-template-name gpu-pool-lt --source-version 3 --launch-template-data file://lt-fix.json`
- Update ASG to use new version: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-asg --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abc123,Version=$NEW_VERSION`
- If new ASG instances still fail to register, manually create one node with the working AMI and attach to the cluster for immediate relief: `aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0gpu-ok --instance-type p4d.24xlarge --iam-instance-profile Name=ec2-k8s`

Maria: I'm taking over oncall. Handoff notes:
- Current hypothesis: Launch template points to deprecated AMI -> instances boot but kubelet fails -> nodes don't join -> autoscaler keeps creating instances until ASG/region limits kick in or backoff occurs.
- Evidence: older AMI name in LT metadata, kubelet logs showing driver/CRI errors.
- Temporary mitigations in flight: new LT version creation (Sophie), manual seed instance (Alex), routing tiered traffic away (Support Ops).

oncall-bot: Handoff registered: Maria now oncall (duration 2h). Incident channel pinned.

Maria: I'll:
- verify LT new version successfully created and that AMI id = `ami-0gpu-updated`.
- bump ASG desired capacity by +4 (cautious) after LT points to updated AMI.
- monitor kubelet journal via `kubectl get nodes -w` and `journalctl -u kubelet` on newly created node via SSM.

Kevin: adding cluster-autoscaler patch to stop tight retry loop temporarily: set `--scale-down-disabled=false` and `--node-group-auto-discovery` retention? Actually we'll patch helm chart to increase `--expander=least-waste`? Suggest throttle the autoscaler to reduce API churn while we fix LT.

Sophie: I pushed new LT version 5 with correct AMI and user-data. ASG updated to version 5 and desired=4. Newly launched instances now show `Registered` at k8s level after ~3m. kubelet logs show the driver loads and node labels `accelerator=nvidia` present.

Maria: good. Observability: queue length started dropping 10m after nodes Ready. Error rate down from 40% -> 8%. Will continue to monitor for 30-60m to ensure stability.

Support Ops: Confirmed top customers now back to normal for new requests; in-flight queued requests are draining, ETA ~18m. Noted one customer reported a failed batch job — reached out to re-run.

Alex: postmortem checklist:
- Root cause: Launch template still referenced deprecated GPU AMI after AMI rotation; change didn't propagate to ASG/launch-template versions and automation didn't detect.
- Contributing factors: terraform/infra race during prior deploy, autoscaler retries masked the underlying AMI error because autoscaler shows create succeeded but node registration failed. No guard that AMI is marked as supported in LT validation.
- Actions: 1) Add CI check to verify LT AMI matches approved GPU AMI list before promotion. 2) Add cluster-autoscaler alert rule for "created instance but node never registered" pattern (currently noisy). 3) Update runbook to include manual seed instance recipe and ASG update steps. 4) Add a deployment-step to atomically update LT and ASG to avoid drift.

Sophie: I will file infra PR for LT validation + add a monthly AMI rotation test job.

Maria: I'll own the incident writeup and postmortem, target within 72h. Also scheduling a 1:1 with infra to review the terraform apply logs and API rate limits that occurred during the prior change.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). Total duration: ~1h20m.

Alex: thanks team. Leaving final note: consider adding a temporary autoscaler fallback to CPU nodes for a subset of lightweight models to reduce blast radius when GPU node joins fail.

Support Ops: Marking customer-facing messages as sent for the 3 affected accounts. We will follow up with SLA credit assessments if required.

Maria: handoff complete — moving to post-incident monitoring.
